decisions.reason: As a flagship digital product line tightly linked to the core practice software and the firm's strategic direction, it remains a valuable option to keep open unless there is clear evidence of persistent weak adoption.

The education institute leverages the installed customer base and training capabilities, but because it is a more peripheral and service-intensive extension than core software it faces a moderate pruning risk rather than immediate abandonment.

The remote support tool complements the firm's support model and is likely inexpensive to maintain, so option logic favors retaining it while its contribution to customer retention and service efficiency continues to justify itself.
A practice analytics dashboard fits closely with the software base and the move toward more digital and efficient practice management, making it a strategically sensible product to continue.
The complete practice bundle is close to the established offer and likely economical to market as a package, so there is little reason to withdraw it unless demand clearly disappoints.

The job and practice listing portal is relatively distant from the firm's core software business and depends on harder-to-build marketplace dynamics, so after several years it is the most likely option to abandon and reallocate resources from.
